subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should OpenClaw keep automatic bare-text delivery for direct/source chats, or change the default/policy so channel-visible source replies require explicit message-tool or final-only semantics?
rationale: The current source and tests preserve automatic direct replies for compatibility, but the issue thread contains multiple production cross-channel leaks where that policy exposes internal assistant text.

options.title: Choose explicit/final-only source delivery
options.body: Make direct/source channel replies safe by default, with tests covering pre-tool, inter-tool, trailing, and cron announce paths plus an upgrade story for existing bare-text DM users.

options.title: Keep automatic direct replies with opt-in guards
options.body: Preserve compatibility as the default and land narrower config or verbose/final-tag mitigations for deployments willing to opt in.

options.title: Defer to candidate PRs only
options.body: Review candidate PRs as incremental mitigations without resolving the broader delivery-default policy in this issue.

recommendation.title: Choose explicit/final-only source delivery
recommendation.body: Make direct/source channel replies safe by default, with tests covering pre-tool, inter-tool, trailing, and cron announce paths plus an upgrade story for existing bare-text DM users.

likelyOwner.reason: The current central code blame in this checkout points to Peter Steinberger across the delivery-mode, embedded-subscriber, and cron-helper paths, making him the best available routing owner for the policy choice.
